rationale: PROPOSAL: add the site-chrome renderer as the fourth call site of the schema-derivation principle this repo has already approved for three. THE DEFECT. Site chrome (header/footer/head) is rendered against a hardcoded map of template values built in Go. render_site_components_action.go:222-262 literally enumerates the vocabulary it will supply - company_name, logo_url, logo_text, nav_items_html, quick_links_html, cta_url, cta_text, legal_links, categories - and :530 renders the component's html_template against exactly that. input_schema appears nowhere in the file; site_components.content_data is never read either. So a chrome component whose schema declares any other field name receives the empty string for every one, silently. The failure is silent BY CONSTRUCTION: component_library.go:544-559 detects Go's output for missing keys, counts it, replaces it with "" and logs only a count with a 100-char template preview. LIVE CONSEQUENCE. idea.uk sits on two per-site fork components (site-header f420f3fa, site-footer 4238e467, created 2026-05-06) declaring nav_link_1_url..nav_link_4_label, cta_primary_url, cta_secondary_url, nav_aria_label, col1_link1_url..col3_link4_label. None is in the map. Today, on the live public site: 30 of 34 anchors on every page render href="" - the entire primary navigation, every CTA, all social links - plus . The site is unnavigable. The proof of mechanism is company_name: it IS in the hardcoded map and it is the ONLY chrome value that rendered. WHY THIS IS STRUCTURAL AND WILL RECUR. The component-creator agent that mints these components is contractually instructed to emit exactly the sources chrome cannot honour: 093_component_creator.sql:1185 makes template and schema 'two views of the same contract' and its TIER C tells generators to write source: site_specs.{path} / site_assets.{type}. The generator therefore produces, by design, schemas the chrome renderer is structurally incapable of resolving - site-header sources its URLs from site_specs.navigation.link_N_url and there is NO navigation aspect in site_specs for ANY of the 11 sites. Nothing will stop the next generated chrome component landing in the same state. Meanwhile the equivalent page-section path (plan_sections_action.go:1210-1218) does apply static fallbacks; chrome is a thinner path that skipped the lessons the section path learned, and store_generated_component_action.go:311-318 already documents this exact silent-blanking mechanism - but guards only page sections. I AM AWARE THIS CONTRADICTS A DEPLOYED DECISION, AND THAT IS THE QUESTION I WANT REVIEWED. LNK-007 (link-management.md:52-58, status deployed) fixed this same hardcoded-ContentData surface by hardcoding MORE - header cta_url resolved from the real contact page, footer legal links data-driven from GetNavItems - and LNK-016 records why: 'Its scope excludes ContentData values and literal anchors - which is why the header/footer phantoms (LNK-007) had to be fixed at source in Go instead.' The vonc link-integrity patch did it a second time in July. Both were right for their moment: they repaired the values the map already supplied. Neither could help a component asking for names the map does not contain, because the map is the ceiling. I am not proposing to undo LNK-007 - its resolved ctaURL stays authoritative - I am proposing to stop the ceiling being fixed. The scope this belongs to is already owner-approved: 'full platform fix (schema-derived CTA pairing, anchor gating, work-item handler, site fix, planner cause)'. PLAN_2026-07-19_cta_link_integrity.md:86-89 names 'one derivation function, three call sites: plan_sections, resolve_internal_links, applyCTARecompute'. The chrome renderer is absent from that list, and RUNBOOK_cta_link_integrity.md:40-42 flags why nobody noticed: the CTA census covers page_components only and 'does not cover site_components (header/footer), so nav dead links are invisible to this census'. This submission adds the missing fourth call site. INTENT AND DELIBERATE CONSERVATISM. Reuse the existing sourceResolver (plan_sections_action.go:65-475, same package, zero new resolution code) so chrome honours what components declare. Two hard limits, both chosen to respect prior decisions rather than override them: (1) schema-resolved values fill GAPS only - wherever the hardcoded map already supplies a non-empty value it stays authoritative, so LNK-007's resolved cta_url and legal links win and the nine working sites render byte-identically; (2) declared fallbacks are applied ONLY for source:static, never on a missed data-source resolution. Limit (2) exists because header-bold-gradient.cta_url declares source pages.contact with fallback /contact.html - NOTES_cta_link_integrity.md:333-336 calls it 'the literal fossil of the 143 of 144 buttons point at /contact.html bug, still in the schema'. Applying that fallback on a miss would resurrect the exact phantom LNK-007 deployed to kill, on nine sites. Leaving it unresolved is LNK-005 (correct-or-absent) by construction. This change does NOT by itself make idea.uk render correctly - its two templates contain zero {{if}} gates, so genuinely-unresolvable fields still emit empty attributes; that is a separate DB-only template fix. What this change buys is that the class stops recurring silently on every future chrome component.

plan.summary: The site-chrome renderer builds a hardcoded map of template values and never reads the component's input_schema, so any chrome component declaring other field names silently receives empty strings - producing 30 dead href="" anchors on every page of idea.uk, live and public, and guaranteed to recur because the component-creator agent is contractually told to emit site_specs.*/site_assets.* sources that chrome cannot resolve. This adds the chrome renderer as the fourth call site of the already-approved schema-derivation principle, reusing sourceResolver from the page-section path (same package, zero new resolution code). Deliberately conservative in two ways that preserve deployed decision LNK-007: resolved values FILL GAPS ONLY so the hardcoded map stays authoritative wherever it supplies a value, and declared fallbacks apply only to source:static, never on a missed data-source resolution - because header-bold-gradient.cta_url's fallback is /contact.html, the fossil of the phantom-CTA bug LNK-007 fixed. Third edit names the residual unresolved fields at render time, replacing a count-only warning that let 30 dead controls ship unnoticed.

edits.rationale: The component's declared schema is never loaded, so it cannot be honoured. Both SELECTs that fetch the template - the assigned-component query (:489-494) and the default-component fallback (:507-512) - must also return input_schema. This edit alone changes no rendering behaviour; it makes the schema available to edit 2.

edits.rationale: The fix. Resolve the schema's declared fields through the EXISTING sourceResolver rather than writing a second resolver: it already handles site_specs.*, site_assets.* (incl. the image-role alias), pages.* and config.*, and already carries the rule that an unresolvable pages.* source returns (nil,false) instead of fabricating a URL - its own comment at plan_sections_action.go:449-453 names URL fabrication as 'the phantom-link generator'. Same package, so no export or refactor; newSourceResolver's doc-comment states an empty pageName 'degrades safely', which is exactly the chrome case (chrome is site-wide, not per-page). TWO DELIBERATE LIMITS, both preserving prior deployed decisions. (a) GAP-FILL ONLY: a schema-resolved value is written only where ContentData has no key or holds an empty string. LNK-007's hardcoded resolutions - the real-contact-page cta_url, the GetNavItems legal links - therefore remain authoritative, and the nine sites on header-bold-gradient/footer-4-column (whose schema field names are all already in the map: cta_text, cta_url, logo_text, logo_url, nav_items, company_name, tagline, copyright, contact_email, contact_phone, primary_color, accent_color) render byte-identically. (b) FALLBACKS ONLY FOR source:static, never on a missed data-source resolution. This is not fastidiousness: header-bold-gradient.cta_url is {source: pages.contact, fallback: /contact.html} - the documented fossil of the '143 of 144 buttons point at /contact.html' bug. Honouring that fallback on a miss would re-fabricate, on nine live sites, precisely the phantom LNK-007 was deployed to remove. Leaving it unresolved so a gated template renders nothing IS invariant LNK-005 ('an unresolvable destination renders nothing rather than a broken link'). The same limit protects logo_url, whose fallback /assets/images/logo.png would otherwise 404 on sites without that asset.

Make the residue loud and specific. After edit 2 some fields legitimately stay unresolved (an llm field never authored; a source with genuinely no data). Today that is indistinguishable from success: component_library.go:552-559 blanks <no value> and logs a COUNT plus a 100-char template preview - which is why 30 dead controls on a live public site produced no actionable signal for months, and why bugs_open/018 records that this 'almost certainly pre-dates the cutover'. Naming the slot, component and FIELD NAMES turns a silent class into a greppable one at the moment it happens, and gives the operator the exact list a template needs to gate. Deliberately a log line and NOT a work item: bugs_open/023 established that this platform's failure mode with this class is a DELIVERY gap - 34 correctly-filed CTA findings sit unread at needs_human_review with zero consumers ('adding more checks without building the handler makes the invisible pile bigger'). A handler is a separate piece of work with its own review.

plan.risks: 1) REGRESSION ON THE NINE WORKING SITES is the thing to check hardest. Two guards: gap-fill-only precedence, and static-only fallbacks. Verify both branches. The overlap set between the hardcoded map and those components' schemas is company_name, logo_url, logo_text, cta_url, cta_text, tagline, copyright, contact_email, contact_phone, nav_items — i.e. ALL of their fields are already in the map, so under gap-fill they are untouched EXCEPT where the map's value is empty. 2) THE ONE REAL BEHAVIOUR CHANGE ON A WORKING SITE is logo_url: sites.logo_url is empty for BOTH idea.uk and vonc.com, and header-bold-gradient declares logo_url source site_assets.logo. So after this change vonc.com may newly render a logo image where it currently falls through to its {{else}} glyph. I believe that is a fix, but it is a visible change to a live site that should be seen coming, not discovered — a reviewer may reasonably ask for site_assets-sourced image fields to be excluded from the first landing. 3) THE FALLBACK RULE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT COSMETIC. If a reviewer 'simplifies' edit 2 by applying def["fallback"] on a missed resolution, header-bold-gradient.cta_url re-fabricates /contact.html across nine live sites and re-opens LNK-007. Any revision touching that branch must be checked against the fossil quote in grounded_in. 4) COST: sourceResolver issues DB queries (ensureSpecs/ensurePages/ensureAssets) and caches per instance; constructing one per slot means up to 3x the loads per site. Hoisting a single resolver into RenderSiteComponentsAction and passing it down is the obvious refinement if a reviewer thinks it matters. 5) THIS DOES NOT FIX THE LIVE SITE BY ITSELF. idea.uk's two templates have zero {{if}} gates (grep -c '{{if' returns 0 on both), so any field that legitimately stays unresolved still emits an empty attribute. Gating them is a DB-only change, out of this gate's scope (platform/ only), and is being done alongside. Do NOT approve this in the belief that it makes idea.uk navigable — its value is that the class stops recurring silently. 6) ORDERING: Go change, inert until a chassis image is rebuilt and rolled; per the 098 precedent the image must be live in-pod BEFORE any accompanying schema/seed change. 7) NO TEST EXISTS for render_site_components_action.go today; a reviewer may reasonably require one covering the gap-fill precedence and the miss-path-does-not-apply-fallback rule, since those two branches are the entire safety argument.
